public_payload.normalized_proposition: Neither Google's TPUs, Amazon's Trainium or Inferentia chips, Vera Rubin CPUs, OpenAI's chips nor DeepSeek will make AI cheaper.

statement.excerpt: Google’s TPUs won’t do it, Amazon’s Trainium or Inferentia chips won’t do it, Vera Rubin CPUs won’t do it, OpenAI’s chips won’t do it, and no, DeepSeek won’t do it either.

from_speaker: Amazon’s Trainium or Inferentia chips won’t do it
Vera Rubin CPUs won’t do it
our_interpretation: Do it refers to making AI cheaper in the preceding sentences.
The ordinary reading is a reduction in the cost of comparable useful AI work attributable to at least one named technology.
The CPU reference is treated as referring to NVIDIA's Vera CPU.
The context concerns producing AI services, so advertised API discounts alone do not establish lower production costs.
Evidence of savings before publication is relevant background but does not by itself establish a post-publication forecast outcome.
criteria.support_condition: A defined comparison could show no savings for a particular deployment. No finite set of unsuccessful deployments establishes that none of these technologies will ever lower costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A post-publication deployment of any named technology demonstrably reduces the cost of comparable AI work.

evidence.excerpt: By migrating BLIP inference on AWS Inferentia-based EC2 Inf2 instances, Tomofun reduced their Furbo application deployment costs by 83%.
evidence.explanation: The customer-coauthored account describes comparable BLIP service after migration from GPU instances and reports maintained performance. It is strong contrary background, but the savings were already reported before Zitron's forecast; the migration date is not specified.

evidence.excerpt: In summary, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash simultaneously improves model intelligence and inference efficiency while reducing deployment costs.
evidence.explanation: The report describes reduced cache storage and other deployment optimizations, providing a concrete technical challenge to the forecast. It does not supply the matched realized task-cost comparison required by this contract.

evidence.excerpt: We also examine failures, human effort, and costs.

evidence.explanation: The study reports one TPU training workload costing 25% less per run, alongside substantial migration failures and correctness risks. This is relevant to broader AI costs but does not establish comparable deployed generative-AI inference savings.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated post-publication deployment showing lower cost for comparable useful AI work attributable to any named technology would contradict the forecast. A narrower workload and deadline would be needed for a conclusive supporting result.
